transcript:
Meeting start 14:00 PDT. Recording on.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Ethan from our SE team is here too. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Lydia Chen: Hey Maya, doing well. Busy quarter. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Markus Olsson: Hi. Morning from Stockholm.
[00:15] Ethan Ross: Morning! Quick agenda: usage/cost highlights, reliability incidents, dedicated vs hosted cost/latency, security questions, then next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Ravi Kapoor: Yep.

--- Summary / quick numbers ---
[00:30] Maya Patel: Quick top-line — Venturis saw ~2.7x growth in tokens since June, and two big late-night peaks that drove bill shock. We flagged the July 29th spike as unusual.
[00:42] Lydia Chen: Right. That week our batch reranker job mis-scheduled, basically reprocessed a big history window, so it re-encoded millions of docs overnight. Should've been backfilled incrementally but we had a scheduler bug.
[00:55] Ethan Ross: That maps to an increase in embedding requests and long context runs. We saw batching break down for some long-sequence calls which increases per-token cost.

--- Incident and reliability discussion ---
[01:10] Markus Olsson: We also noticed increased tail latencies around 02:00UTC — P95/P99 spikes. Any idea what caused that?
[01:18] Ethan Ross: From our traces, two things: cross-tenant noisy neighbors on shared pool during your bursts and the KV cache miss rate increased for long histories. Essentially prefix caching wasn't effective because the queries had high variability.
[01:34] Lydia Chen: When you say "K-V cash" — you mean KV cache right? Sorry the auto transcript wrote cash earlier.
[01:38] Ethan Ross: Yeah KV cache. And on the shared hosted environment the batching windows can be wider to improve throughput but that can hurt latency for single-shot low-token requests.
[01:48] Maya Patel: Important tradeoff. This is where Dedicated helps — predictable pool, isolated GPU, you can set autoscale behavior and cap burst policies.

--- Dedicated vs Hosted economics ---
[01:56] Markus Olsson: We want hard numbers. If we commit to a dedicated pool for peak traffic, what are the cost deltas, and how do we handle underutilization?
[02:06] Maya Patel: We'll share a spreadsheet, but high level: Dedicated has higher base cost (reserved GPU hours) but PPU (per-processing-unit) cost per token drops and P95 latency becomes stable. For your workload with high nightly batch, the committed plan often breaks even within 8–12 weeks versus burst on hosted.
[02:22] Lydia Chen: Is there an option for burst on hosted plus a small dedicated pool to cover tails?
[02:26] Ethan Ross: Yes, hybrid routing is supported — policy-based routing by latency and cost. We can keep most inference on hosted, route priority traffic to Dedicated. Also automatic fallback to hosted if the dedicated pool is full.

--- Networking, VPC, and egress ---
[02:38] Ravi Kapoor: Network is a big concern — our security team wants VPC peering for private connections. If embeddings or vector indices are generated via your hosted API, what's the expected egress and how does that show up on the bill?
[02:50] Maya Patel: If you use hosted API, egress to your storage or client is charged by cloud egress at your cloud provider rates — Redwood shows token and data transfer breakdown in the console, but we can run numbers if you share your expected document sizes. For private deployments (Redwood Private), data stays in your VPC and egress is internal — different model and usually a platform fee plus support license.
[03:12] Markus Olsson: So for on-prem or VPC we get more control, but there's a larger operational overhead?
[03:18] Ethan Ross: Correct. Private deployments require customer-managed infra and we provide the control plane and packages. There's an initial setup and ops handover — often chosen by regulated customers.

--- Compliance & Auditability ---
[03:28] Lydia Chen: We're under a contractual security review — need SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS details. Can you provide sample logs and evidence of retention windows?
[03:37] Maya Patel: Absolutely — I'll send the security pack. It includes our SOC2 Type II summary, sample audit log export format, SSO integrations, RBAC notes, and KMS/HSM encryption workflow.
[03:46] Markus Olsson: We also want to verify data residency and retention options — can we configure retention per model or per workspace?
[03:54] Ethan Ross: There's workspace-level retention controls in the Console, and for Private deployments you can set policies in your environment. Hosted has configurable retention tiers and legal hold options.

--- Evals and quality regressions ---
[04:06] Lydia Chen: On quality: after a backend model swap in mid-August we saw an uptick in short hallucinations in our reranker. Any rollbacks or guardrails?
[04:16] Ethan Ross: We do model version pinning and can do canary rollouts per route. We recommend shipping small rollouts with evaluation sets; Redwood Optimize can run prompt-based regression checks and alert if quality drops beyond thresholds.
[04:30] Lydia Chen: Good — we'll need that on by default for rerankers.

--- Pricing nuance and discounts ---
[04:36] Markus Olsson: Contractually, how do committed discounts work? If we commit to 6 months, what's the delta?
[04:42] Maya Patel: Typically we offer tiered discounts on committed spend. Exact numbers depend on committed GPU-hours and token tiers. I'll include a committed discount worksheet showing break-evens for your projected growth profiles.

--- Deep dive: benchmarking asked by Venturis ---
[05:02] Ravi Kapoor: For the benchmark, we need raw latencies (cold start, warm, P50/P95/P99) at our burst scale. Can Redwood reproduce something close to our traffic?
[05:10] Ethan Ross: Yes — ask you to provide representative prompt sets and traffic distribution. We'll run a 48-hour stress benchmark with both hosted and dedicated configurations and share the raw traces + a summary sheet with kernel-level metrics where possible.

--- Clarifications, mis-transcripts, and cross-talk ---
[05:28] Lydia Chen: Quick note — if you see any odd words in the transcript (like "K-V cash"), that's our internal note, ignore it.
[05:34] Maya Patel: Yep, thanks for flagging.

--- Recap and explicit next steps live ---
[05:40] Maya Patel: To recap, action items we agreed: Redwood to send security pack and pricing workbook; SE to run 48h stress; Venturis to share traffic and prompt sets; schedule SRE canary review later this month.
[05:56] Markus Olsson: Works. One more ask — can Redwood include a sample canary policy configuration so our infra team can comment ahead of the follow-up?
[06:04] Ethan Ross: Yes, we'll include a sample canary config and an example of automatic fallback to hosted.

--- Closing small talk and wrap ---
[06:12] Lydia Chen: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the follow-through.
[06:16] Maya Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with the docs by next week.
[06:20] Ravi Kapoor: Thanks, bye.
[06:22] Meeting end (recording stopped).

Notes: transcript contains typical auto-caption issues; timestamps are approximate. The call included both AE-led commercial discussion and SE-led technical commitments. The recording will be attached to the CRM.
